source_contract.title: On the regularization mechanism for the periodic Korteweg-de Vries equation
hypotheses: The torus has length 2*pi, the datum is real and mean-zero.
The horizon Q is positive and the nonnegative Sobolev regularity and initial norms are as stated.
source_contract.context: Source Sections 3-4 specify the homogeneous normalized norms and the coefficient solution notion. Theorem 4.2 gives uniform Galerkin bounds, 4.3 the limiting solution for positive s, 5.1 uniqueness and continuity for s>1/2, 6.3 for 0<s<=1/2, 6.4 for s=0. Uniformity on norm-bounded sets is the quantitative content of the estimates in their proofs, not a new hypothesis.
source_contract.source_statement: Imported exact-flow clauses of the cited theorem suite: Theorem 4.2: if v^(m)(0)=v0 in dot H^s0, s0>=0, ||v^(m)(0)||_(dot H^0)<=M0 and T>0, then ||v^(m)(t)||_(dot H^s0)<=M_s0 on [0,T], uniformly in m, where M_s0 depends only on M0,T,||v0||_(dot H^s0),s0. Theorem 4.3: for s0>0, v0 in dot H^s0,T>0,0<sigma<s0, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,T];H^sigma), 1<p<infinity, and weak-* in L^infinity dot H^s0 to a solution of (3.8) in Definition 3.1, bounded by M_s0, with dot H^0 norm equal to its initial norm a.e. Theorem 5.1: for s>1/2 that solution is unique, C([0,T];dot H^s), Lipschitz in initial data as in (5.18), and conserves dot H^0 for all t. Theorem 6.3: for 0<s<=1/2 it is unique, C([0,T];dot H^s), and Lipschitz as in (6.7). Theorem 6.4: for s=0 there is a unique C([0,T];dot H^0) solution depending Lipschitz continuously on its data. Section 3 identifies these coefficient solutions with the physical U_t=UU_x+U_xxx; the proofs construct them by Galerkin or smooth limits.
source_contract.notation_map: The source physical field is called U here; source twisted coefficients are z_k=exp(i*k^3*t)*hat U(k). Its normalized homogeneous Sobolev norms agree with Hdot. The reflection/sign bridge to our KdV is proved in N001.

source_contract.statement: For the real mean-zero periodic equation U_t=U*U_x+U_xxx on ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), use hat U(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral U(x)exp(-i*k*x)dx, ||U||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2s)|hat U(k)|^2, and z_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t)hat U(t)(k). For every s>0 and horizon Q>0, every initial datum U_0 in dot H^s has a distributional solution with z in C([0,Q];dot H^s), unique in the source solution class (z in L^infinity dot H^0 satisfying z_k(t)-z_k(0)=(i*k/2)integral_0^t sum_(k1+k2=k)exp(i*3*k*k1*k2*r)z_k1(r)z_k2(r)dr). Its dot H^0 norm is conserved, and the flow depends Lipschitz continuously on the initial data in dot H^s, uniformly on bounded dot H^s sets on [0,Q]. The Galerkin approximations (with the nonlinear inputs and output projected to |k|<=m and high coefficients frozen) have dot H^s bounds uniform in m, depending only on s,Q, the initial dot H^s norm and an upper bound for the initial dot H^0 norm. For 0<sigma<s they admit a subsequence converging strongly in L^q([0,Q];dot H^sigma), 1<q<infinity, and weak-* in L^infinity dot H^s to this solution; the same dot H^s bound holds for the limit. For s=0 there is a unique C([0,Q];dot H^0) solution, conserving that norm and depending Lipschitz continuously on its data. These flows agree on overlapping regularity classes and are obtained by smooth approximation.
